hypothesis: A long-lived trend can contain temporary negative price dislocations. Buy only when a causal autoregression of the detrended log-price residual forecasts enough reversion to cover stressed roundtrip costs; reject collapsing or non-mean-reverting regimes.
execution: Root common evaluator: next available daily open with adverse execution price and fees. Signals never use the future open.

mathematics.trend: Causal exponentially weighted moving average of log close, alpha = 2 / (trend_span + 1).
mathematics.residual: r_t = log(close_t) - EMA_t; every past residual uses only its own available history.
mathematics.fit: Ordinary least squares r_j = a + phi * r_(j-1) + epsilon_j over a fixed trailing fit window.
mathematics.cost_hurdle: gross_forecast >= edge_multiple * (log(1.01 / 0.99) + log(1.001 / 0.999)); the same exact log-cost hurdle for 100-bps fees and 10-bps slippage per side applies to every execution-cost scenario.
mathematics.regime: 0.2 < phi < 0.98, configured half-life bounds, positive finite innovation variance, and the 20-day log-trend change above the configured floor.
mathematics.exit: At a completed close, leave when residual z >= -0.1, regime/fit becomes invalid, maximum holding days elapse, or log return from the signal reference close <= -max(0.04, 2.5 * entry_stationary_scale).

risk.allocation: One global long position. When flat and both instruments qualify, choose the highest forecast gross return divided by stationary residual scale; ties use symbol order. Hold that instrument until an explicit exit.
risk.intraday_stop_assumption: None. Exits are evaluated on closed candles and execute on a later open, so overnight gaps and delayed exits remain possible.
risk.warmup: At least max(trend_span, fit_window + 1, 21) observations. EMA begins at the first observed log close.

selection.objective: Highest development stress net profit minus 0.5 times maximum dollar drawdown, with root-defined activity eligibility.
selection.future_outcomes: No validation or final-period outcomes inspected during model design or selection. Historical periods have been reused in older research and are not claimed to be virgin holdouts.
